House & shed model assumptions

Photo-informed low-poly house: two-storey south-facing main gable, shallow hipped front porch roof, west bay with a small hipped roof, square porch posts, three upper front windows and right-side entry. Main eaves/ridge are estimated at 18/25 ft; rear mass at 16/21.5 ft. The covered west and north porch roofs slope away from the house and meet at a continuous diagonal hip; open and enclosed sections share the same roof surfaces. Rear roof junctions and lower extensions are simplified assumptions, not measured roof geometry. Ground-level footprint follows the approximate survey trace. Calculation details & assumptions

Transitions & shared posts

Distances start at the shared northeast corner. The height-transition handles control the length of 4 ft fencing toward the street; 6 ft fencing begins at the northeast corner. The short section stays fixed in feet when total length changes, clamped to the available run length. East and North controls are mirrored to match the plan.

Each nonempty height section is split into equal bays no longer than maximum spacing. A post is placed exactly at the transition; it serves both heights and is sized for the taller section. The northeast corner is counted once and uses the taller adjacent section. Posts = total bays + 1, or zero when no runs are active.

Boards & footings

Pickets are rounded up separately for each section: (length × 12 + gap) ÷ (width + gap). Face-mounted boards cover the full section; post widths are not subtracted. Rails = bays × rails per bay for that height, with stock length rounded up to the next 2 ft. No reuse of offcuts is assumed.

Post stock covers section height plus hole depth minus gravel, rounded up to the next 2 ft. Concrete subtracts the square post volume from the circular footing. Waste is applied to each stock group before rounding; concrete bags are pooled across all holes. Spare posts do not add footings.

Survey context & limits

The lot uses the survey's 61.50 × 101.50 ft edges and 90°56′ southwest angle. The house outline is an approximate orthogonal fit to a traced scan; lighter shapes are porches. Streets are schematic, muted bands extended beyond the 3D view. Camera framing follows the house, not the road extents. Model axes follow Oakwood, not geodetic bearings.

Confirm boundaries, permits, utility marking, soil, wind, frost and construction details. Survey geometry does not establish legal fence height. Rail size, lumber availability, fasteners, cut details, slope and ground clearance require verification. No gates, demolition, labor or delivery included.
